Big Beverage capacity - potential Alani volume share (2 lines)
Big Beverage potential Alani volume capacity

Eight weeks into Eric Hansen's tenure as first President & COO (28-year PepsiCo veteran); company framed as being at a 'pivotal point' with a two-brand portfolio (Celsius + Alani Nu) at ~16-17% combined share.

Q1 2025 revenue softness framed as 'noise' - innovation timing shifting later in the quarter vs. front-loaded in Q1 2024, lapping the Essentials launch, promotional timing, and a tough ~35-37% prior-year comp.
Core Celsius has shown 'a couple of months of week-over-week growth in dollars' and is 'working its way back'; Alani Nu described as 'currently a rocket ship.'
Core Celsius dollar share down slightly YoY (~11%); management notably declined to reaffirm a prior ~15% Celsius share goal, pivoting to combined ~17% portfolio share and channels already over 20%.

Retailer feedback flagged 'too many flavors'; management conceded the need to rationalize SKUs and improve ACV on top sellers - best sellers under-distributed (Orange at 84 ACV vs. company 98; top 10 SKUs should be 90%+).

SKU rationalization and set right-sizing planned toward year-end - reduces complexity, helps both top line and bottom-line margin; 2025 reset plans largely locked, further space gains a 2026 opportunity.

Q1 gross margin above 52% (up ~100 bps); full-year pegged ~50% explicitly as 'conservatism' against unknown tariffs (better that week, peaked around the earnings call) and expected commodity/aluminum inflation - not a known cost headwind.

Aluminum's share of COGS not quantified - 'consistent with the beverage category'; mitigation via going direct on raw materials, using co-packers differently, multiple toolbox levers over coming years.

$50M of Alani Nu synergies identified (significant portion headcount - built-out sales and supply-chain teams); 12-month transition service agreement; ~18-month integration runway after which Alani Nu's P&L converges to Celsius's.
Alani Nu modeling call targeted for Memorial Day week (~late May 2025) - pro forma combined-business detail and purchase-accounting framing.
A new Celsius marketing campaign launches within ~30 days, timed to capture summer growth and refocus on the core Celsius consumer.
Celsius launching its first national, all-channel limited-time-offer (winter theme) in the back half - a test of the Alani Nu-style LTO playbook applied to Celsius; expects to repeat if successful.

Big Beverage fully integrated and kitted for a second line; as Alani Nu grows, ~20-25% of its current volume could move in-house; Celsius runs a six-orbit model (6 primary plants + ~6-7 secondary), could double capacity within the current footprint, and is not in any Pepsi plants.

Alani Nu's biggest positive surprise was its marketing capability - opportunity to combine the strengths of the Celsius and Alani Nu marketing teams into data-driven, consumer-focused teams; brand teams kept separate to preserve each brand's voice.
Better-for-you/zero-sugar now over 50% of the category, creating more permissibility and bringing more consumers in; energy sourcing volume from older categories - tea, water, juice, coffee, dairy.

Pricing: Celsius took headline Q4 2024 pricing to 'get it' but has been promoting much of it back; a recent singles-vs-multipack mix shift created an optical price uplift in scanner data that is really just mix; pricing remains a future optionality lever.

Combined-portfolio distribution expected to expand 15-20% in 2025 - from set growth at large customers, Subway (~18,000 stores), Home Depot, ~15,000 additional small-format coolers, energy space growth within total beverage, independent-set increases in the Pepsi system; Walmart energy-space expansion timing 'TBD.'

International: a huge runway (Monster ~40% vs. Celsius ~5% incl. Alani), deliberate 'build' approach not a shotgun approach; building EMEA resources including a global operations team in Dublin; performance largely in line, 'probably more to the upside.'
M&A: focus is integration and paying down debt; would look at the right opportunity but sees ample runway to build out the portfolio.
Revenue management is at a base level with a lot of room to grow - different pack configurations/sizes can drive frequency and occasions.
Confirmed it was the moderator's inaugural event and that Hansen was eight weeks into his role.
What led Hansen to Celsius after a long PepsiCo career, and the company's strengths and opportunities.

Having helped bring Celsius into the PepsiCo system gave a head start on people, culture, brands. Energy is one of the best categories; Celsius/Alani Nu fantastic, fast-growing brands. Strengths in brand-building, consumer/media engagement, field selling, supply chain. Biggest opportunity: reorganizing from a 'one brand-focused, very US-centric' structure toward a portfolio-oriented, global one.
Whether anything surprised Hansen, positive or negative.
Alani Nu's marketing capability was the biggest positive surprise; opportunity to combine the strengths of the Celsius and Alani Nu marketing teams into better, data-driven, consumer-focused teams.
What drives recent category acceleration and where the category is sourcing volume from.

A ton of innovation (especially into zero sugar, now over 50% of the category), consumers seeking more function, and a closing price gap making energy a relatively better value. Volume sourcing from softness in tea, water, juice, coffee - 'older categories' (teas, dairy, juices) higher in sugar and seen as less healthy.
Unpack the Q1 top-line moving parts (distributor incentive timing, promotional allowances, lapping Essentials) and characterize the underlying Q1 growth trend.

Q1 had a lot of noise - innovation front-loaded in Q1 2024 vs. later in Q1 2025, the Essentials launch not repeated, different promotional timing, vs. a tough ~35-37% prior-year comp. Recent trends show a couple of months of week-over-week dollar growth for core Celsius, 'working its way back'; softer comps, year-round innovation timing, a back-half LTO and Alani Nu's strength set up 'a pretty good year.'
Details on the LTO flavor, distribution and channel rollout.
It will be a national, all-channel LTO with a winter theme.
What is weighing on core Celsius share gains (just under 11%, down slightly YoY, stable vs. Q4) and what the company could do better.

Attributed partly to the Essentials lap and changed innovation timing. Focus areas: a fall LTO (vs. traditional front-of-year SKU launches), a marketing campaign launching within ~30 days targeting the core Celsius consumer, and right-sizing flavor sets toward year-end - giving confidence that share momentum returns.
Retailer feedback that there are too many flavors - whether management would rationalize.

Agreed: best sellers are under-distributed (Orange at 84 ACV vs. company 98; top 10 SKUs should be 90%+), so sharper execution on best flavors is needed; rationalization reduces complexity across packages/formats, helping both top line and bottom-line margin.
Whether a prior ~15% Celsius share goal is still achievable and by when.

Hansen declined to confirm a specific goal, noting collective portfolio share is 17% with several markets/channels/customers already over 20%, with runway to move total-US share higher; Langhans added food and retail combined is over 20%.
What Alani Nu (line share 5.3, up >200 bps) is doing better and how Celsius can leverage those learnings.

Two things: continued growth in total points of distribution/ACV, and a very sharp marketing and LTO strategy - deep consumer knowledge, design/flavor focus, social/influencer communication, rotating a new SKU every 2-3 months to create news, excitement and a 'treasure hunt' dynamic with merchandise drops, generating social-media and purchase spikes.
Whether, if the fall Celsius LTO goes well, the company will do more LTOs on the Celsius brand.
Yes, he would expect to do that.
Brand Interaction & Alani Nu Synergies / P&L
How the two brands interact, anything surprising since closing, the modeling-call date, and initial synergies/P&L flow-through opportunities.

Too early to tell since most in-market plans were set before Celsius took control, but ownership gives optionality on price-pack and promotional strategy and how/whether to merchandise the brands together. Modeling call targeted for Memorial Day week; $50M of synergies (significant portion headcount; 12-month TSA); a marketing/brand team carved out to preserve Alani Nu's voice; supply-chain synergies. Alani Nu a couple of years behind Celsius on the P&L profile but fully expected to converge, with integration plus synergies driven over ~18 months.
How Essentials performed vs. internal expectations, where it fell short, current distribution, and the runway ahead.

Largely in line with expectations - a little stronger out of the gate, then stabilizing as anticipated. Distribution opportunity remains (ACV mid-60s, especially in convenience-and-gas) and an opportunity to sharpen brand messaging in performance energy; should continue performing fairly well.
Update on pricing strategy and how it flows through the year, given Q4 2024 pricing was promoted back.

Has been promoting a lot of the pricing back. A recent mix shift with singles growing faster than multipacks creates an optical price uplift in the data that is really just mix. Took the headline price to 'get it,' has been promotional with it; remains a future optionality lever.
Why management is more cautious on the second half (~50% full-year peg vs. 52%+ Q1) - assuming tariffs.

Called the caution 'a bit of conservatism' given uncertainty over tariffs (better that week, at their peak around the earnings call). Cited mitigation strategies in place in advance, some conservatism, and expected commodity inflation - wanting to set a realistic goal.
What percentage of COGS is aluminum, and beyond pricing what mitigation levers exist.

Did not have the aluminum-as-%-of-COGS figure but said it is consistent with the beverage category. Mitigation: leveraging the business to expand margins (citing the larger public competitor's playbook) - going direct on raw materials, using co-packers differently, multiple toolbox tools over coming years.
Alani Nu Margin Accretion & Big Beverage / Space
Whether Alani Nu is accretive with scale/margin advantages, how the integrated Big Beverage facility drives margin lift, and where the 15-20% space expansion comes from.

Alani Nu shares many ingredients, enabling scale and better pricing over coming years plus synergies and margin convergence. Big Beverage has margin savings and is kitted for a second line; as Alani Nu grows, a portion of its volume moves in-house. The 15-20% space expansion comes from set growth at large customers, Subway, Home Depot (~18,000 stores), ~15,000 additional small-format coolers, energy space growth within total beverage, and independent-set increases in the Pepsi system; 2025 plans largely locked, further gains a 2026 opportunity.
Whether all of Alani Nu would move into Big Beverage and how insourcing more volume interacts with the Pepsi relationship.

Not all of Alani Nu - with two lines, Big Beverage holds ~20-25% of current volumes (~25% of current capacity). Celsius is not in any Pepsi plants; runs a six-orbit model (6 primary plants incl. Big Beverage, plus ~6-7 secondary) and could double capacity within the current footprint; has explored opportunities with Pepsi (partly around tunnel-pasteurizing sourcing/footprint).
Pepsi / Alani Nu Distribution & International Strategy
Whether Pepsi would distribute Alani Nu, and how Celsius drives daily consumption internationally and balances US vs. global expansion.

Current focus is resets and ensuring product is on shelf; sees opportunities with both distribution systems but nothing to announce. On international, the focus is building deliberately in markets already entered, not a 'shotgun approach,' with performance roughly in line; a huge runway (Monster ~40% vs. Celsius ~5% incl. Alani). Building out EMEA resources including a global operations team in Dublin to bring on new countries faster.
Whether international performance has surprised to the upside.
A bit of both - a couple of markets doing better, a couple needing to get on track - but largely in line, 'probably more to the upside.'
What management hears about Walmart's energy-drink space and Langhans's view on future acquisitions.

Not hearing much, but expects Walmart sets to get bigger over time, timing 'TBD.' Company has plenty to keep it busy - integration, paying down debt, a strong back-half/summer plan plus global expansion; Eric's structuring work sets the company up to do more; would look at the right opportunity but has ample runway with the current portfolio.
